chapter_theme: Dharana (தாரணை): fixing the mind and breath within, through the spine to the head, the yogi sees the dance and the light of bliss, rouses the power at the base, and holds life, body and time still; since all who came before have died, the work is now, and its end is holding the dissolved tattvas in the Supreme.
structure_note: Methods of fixing mind and breath (588, 591 to 595), visions and the rousing of the power (589, 590), a warning that the body will not last (596), and a definition of dharana as the involution of the tattvas (597).

588.reading: For those who fix the unwavering mind, bind it below, look up through the spine into the space above and stay as eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, this is the way that stops the days of life from running out.
588.nuance: வீணாத்தண்டு (the vina's stem) is traditionally the spine. கோணா மனம் may be the mind that does not bend, or the crooked mind to be bound. வாணாள் அடைக்கும் can mean closing off lifespan, so the verse may promise long life or the end of embodied life.

589.reading: A heavenly waterfall flows steadily from the mountain's peak through the long nadi; in the hall the holy dance goes on, and I saw the light of unending bliss.
589.nuance: The plain landscape and the symbolic body both stand: the mountain-top as the head, the waterfall as the nectar of the yogis, the hall (பொது) as the dance-hall of Siva. சிலையார் may mean of stone or of the bow.

590.reading: The girl of the upper region, the transmuting maiden, rouses the form that rises from the root region; when he meets her, he becomes a youth: this is Paranandi's command.
590.nuance: Usually kundalini is the female power that rises from the base to Siva above; here the girl is above and the form rising from the root is male, so the roles may be reversed or my reading wrong. வேதகம் is alchemical transmutation. பாலனும் ஆவான் may mean he becomes a child, as in the return to youth of 569.

591.reading: Those who bind the last door, rouse the breath, look to the middle door, settle sweetly within and wait like a heron at the sluice-mouth may stay unbroken for an aeon.
591.nuance: The last and middle doors are traditionally the anus and the central channel (sushumna). The heron at the sluice (மடைவாய்க் கொக்கு) waits motionless for its moment.

592.reading: If the life joined with the body knows time, the life so joined is the pressure of the breath; if that breath is bound, the life, body and time of the one so joined stand still.
592.nuance: The verse plays on கால், which means both breath and time (காலம்). Each line begins with கலந்த உயிர் (the joined life). The reading is tentative.

593.reading: Those who don't open the mouth have a treasure in the mind; those who open it drive it out with breath; those who keep it closed kindle it with the moon; if the inner door is not opened, one becomes weak.
593.nuance: Nearly every key word is unclear. மாடு may be wealth or an ox; மதி may be the moon or the mind; கோய் is obscure; கோழை may be phlegm or a coward. The verse seems to praise silence and inner practice, and I can't do more than that.

594.reading: One may live for many ages if the breath that splits within the mind is driven inward without escaping; the body has seven windows and two great doors, a large cave and a bedchamber.
594.nuance: The second half is a riddle of the body as a house: seven openings in the head and two below, perhaps. பாழி and பள்ளியறை may be the inner space where Siva rests. எழுசாலேகம் is read as seven lattice windows.

595.reading: When five of the full ten have gone, what will you do, fool, waking and lamenting? For those who mark out a boundary and make a way, it is possible to bag the monkey.
595.nuance: The ten are traditionally the ten vital airs, five of which leave at death. The monkey is the restless mind. கொட்டை பொதியலும் is obscure; the variant கோட்டை (fort) gives 'shut the monkey in a fort'.

596.reading: All who came before have ended; what assurance is there for those who came after? If one talks of crores of states to come, what a trick: will a crumbling bank stand?
596.nuance: The crumbling bank (இடிகரை) is the body. உறுகதி may be states or destinies hoped for after death, which the verse mocks as reasons to wait. The verse's place in the chapter suggests it urges the practice now.

597.reading: Placing the dissolved body in the five elements, the five elements going into sound and the other subtle elements, and the mind and the rest going into what lies beyond them: dharana is holding it all with the Supreme.
597.nuance: The verse runs the tattvas backward, each into its cause. சத்தாதி appears twice, for the subtle elements and for something higher; the repetition may be a corruption. தற்பரம் is the Supreme.

links.note: Both use the heron that waits motionless: in the Kural it is the king biding his time before striking, in Tirumular the yogi who holds still in breath and mind.
Both say no one who came before has escaped death: the Naladiyar shows it in kings under their umbrellas, Tirumular in all who came before.
580 places the coiled kundalini at the root; 590 has the power rising from the root region roused and joined above, with the return to youth as its fruit.

588 tells the yogi to fix the mind and stay as eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear (காணாக்கண் கேளாச் செவி) to stop life's days running out. 1610 says Nandi came and showed an eye that does not see and a hearing that does not hear (காணாத கண்ணுடன் கேளாத கேள்வியும்) together with the awareness at nada's end. The same paradox is a practice the yogi takes on in 588 and a gift shown by the teacher in 1610.

583 gives a method (close the lower door, mind on the upper door, eyes open to the void) and calls it the way to conquer time (காலத்தை வெல்லும்). 592 explains why it works by the pun on கால் as breath and time: the life is the pressure of the breath, and if the breath is bound (காலது கட்டின்) the body's time stands still (காலமும் நிற்குமே). 592 gives the reason behind 583's promise.

593 says those who do not open the mouth (வாய்திறவாதார்) hold a treasure in the mind, and those who open it drive it out with breath. 1780 places the object the teacher told him to think on daily below the crown and above the uvula, held with the mouth not opened (வாய்திற வாதே). The closed mouth is in both a condition of inner practice, which helps fix the sense of the obscure 593.

595 asks the fool what he will do when five of the ten (ஈரைந்தில் ஐந்து, the vital airs) have gone, and says those who make a way can bag the monkey of the mind. Thiruppugazh 1036 counts the breaths by hundreds and thousands by which the little life runs out (ஓடுஞ் சிறுவுயிர்) and asks whether the good yoga that turns it back (மீளும்படி நல யோகம்) is not to be had. Both set the running-out of breath against a yoga that can still be practised, one as warning, the other as prayer.

source_issues: 590: a variant reads பார்நந்தி for பராநந்தி.
595: a variant reads கோட்டைப் (fort) for கொட்டை, which changes the image of confining the monkey.
597: சத்தாதி appears in lines 2 and 3 for what seem to be two different levels; one may be a corruption.
